content.text: Hello everyone and welcome back to EnglishPod. My name is Marco. My name is Catherine and today we have an upper intermediate level lesson for all of you.
content.trans: 你好，大家欢迎再次回到英语有声课堂。我的名字是Marco，我的名字是Catherine，今天我们要进行一门中级上进阶级别的课程，所有学员都可参加。

content.text: That's right. We're going to be talking business on this occasion on EnglishPod but specifically about planning a business.
content.trans: 没错。这次我们将在英语中讨论关于业务的话题，具体来说是关于计划一个生意的。

content.text: Right. So before a business opens, a lot of planning has to happen. That means people will decide what kind of product they want to sell, what kind of a market they want to sell to, etc.
content.trans: 好的。所以，一个生意开之前，很多事情都需要规划。这意味着人们会决定他们想要销售的产品类型，以及他们希望销售给什么样的市场。

content.text: So that is the focus of today's lesson. Let's take a listen to the dialogue for the first time and we'll be back in a minute to talk about what's going on.
content.trans: 所以今天这节课的重点是什么呢？让我们第一次听这个对话，然后我们一会儿再来聊聊发生了什么。

content.text: I've had it. I'm done working for a company that is taking me nowhere. So what are you going to do? Just quit? That's exactly what I'm going to do. I've decided to create my own company. I'm going to write up a business plan, get some investors and start working for myself.
content.trans: 我已经厌倦了。我决定不再为一个让我无处可去的公司工作。那么，你打算怎么做？只是辞职吗？那正是我要做的。我已经决定自己创办一家公司。我会写一份商业计划书，寻找投资者，并开始独立工作。

content.text: Have you ever written up a business plan before? Well, no. It can't be that hard. I mean all you have to do is explain your business. How are you going to do things and that's it, right?
content.trans: 你曾经写过商业计划书吗？没有吧。这应该不难。我意思是，你只需要解释你的业务是什么，然后怎么去做，对不对？

content.text: You can't be more wrong. A well written business plan will include an executive summary which highlights the idea of the business in two pages or less. Then you need to describe your company with information such as what type of legal structure it has, history, etc.
content.trans: 你完全错了。一份好的商业计划书应该包括一个执行摘要，该摘要简要概述了业务的idea，在两页或更少的页面内。然后你需要描述你的公司，提供信息如其法律结构、历史等。

content.text: Well, that seems easy enough. Wait, there's more. Then you need to introduce and describe your goods or services, what they are and how they're different from competitors. Then comes the hard part, a market analysis. You need to investigate and analyze hundreds of variables.
content.trans: 好的，那似乎很简单。等一下，还有更多。然后你需要介绍和描述你的商品或服务，它们是什么以及与其他竞争者有何不同之处。接下来是难的部分，市场分析。你需要调查并分析数百个变量。

content.text: You need to take into consideration socio-economic factors from GDP per capita to how many children on average the population has. All this information is useful so that you can move on to your strategy and implementation stage where you will describe in detail how you will actually execute your idea.
content.trans: 你必须考虑从人均国内生产总值到平均每个人口有多少孩子的社会经济因素。所有这些信息都是有用的，这样你可以进入你的策略和实施阶段，在这个阶段中你将详细描述如何实际执行你的想法。

content.text: Geez, is that all? Almost. The most important piece of information for your investors will be the financial analysis. Here you will calculate and estimate sales, cash flow and profits. After all, people will want to know when they will begin to see a return on their investment.
content.trans: 哎呀，这差不多就完了。最重要的投资者信息就是财务分析。你会计算和估计销售、现金流以及利润的。毕竟人们想知道什么时候开始能从他们的投资中获得回报。

content.text: I think I'll just stick to my old job and save myself all the hassle of trying to start up a business.
content.trans: 我觉得我干脆就继续做我原来的工作，免得自己折腾开办公司的一切麻烦。

content.text: Alright, we're back. So the guy wanted to open up a business, but his friend explained that it's not so easy and gave a lot of interesting words and phrases there.
content.trans: 好的，我们又回来了。这位男士想开个生意，但他的朋友解释说这并不容易，并且给了他很多有趣的话和短语。

content.text: He did. He seemed a little naive. Like he didn't really know how much work is involved in opening a business.
content.trans: 他做了。看起来他还有点天真。好像他真的不知道开一家生意需要投入多少工作量。

content.text: Exactly. So I think we should take a look at some of the words used on language takeaway.
content.trans: Exactly. 我认为我们应该看看语言取餐中使用的某些词汇。

content.text: The first word is the heart and soul of the process before you open a business. It's the business plan.
content.trans: 第一步，你打开业务之前，是整个过程的灵魂和核心。它就是商业计划书。

content.text: Alright, so the business plan, as you said, it's a noun and it's basically a document that explains what's going on in the business.
content.trans: 好的，所以你们所说的商业计划书，它就是一个名词，是一个解释企业在经营中发生的事情的文档。

content.text: Exactly. It's a paper that you write about the business that you want to open and it's a plan.
content.trans: Exactly。它是一张你写给想要开设的业务计划书的纸，是一个计划。

content.text: So that's what the name says. You have to tell what you will do, how much money you will spend, how much money you will need.
content.trans: 所以这就是名字的意思。你必须说清楚你要做什么，要花多少钱，需要多少钱。

content.text: Because if you're asking people for money, they want to know where the money will be spent if it's going to be spent on wise decisions.
content.trans: 因为如果你要求别人出钱，他们想知道这笔钱将花在什么地方，如果真的要花在明智的决策上。

content.text: Exactly. And as you mentioned, so you show this business plan maybe to a bank, but also maybe to an investor.
content.trans: Exactly. 既然你提到过，那么你可以把这个商业计划展示给银行，也可以展示给投资者。

content.text: That's right. So investor is our next word. It's another noun, but this noun is a person.
content.trans: 正确。所以投资者是我们下一个单词。这是一个名词，但这个名词是一个人。

content.text: A person is an investor if he or she gives money to someone else and expects more money to come back.
content.trans: 一个人是投资者，如果他或她将钱借给他人，并期望得到更多的回报。

content.text: Right. So a person that's starting out of business maybe has enough money himself to open up a business, but sometimes you need extra money.
content.trans: 好的。所以，一个刚开始创业的人可能自己有足够的钱开公司，但有时候你确实需要额外的钱。

content.text: So you look for investors, people who are interested in giving you money.
content.trans: 所以你去找投资者，那些对给你钱感兴趣的人。

content.text: For example, I have a cupcake company. I want to sell cupcakes to people and I need a thousand dollars.
content.trans: 例如，我有一个蛋糕公司。我想向人们出售蛋糕，并且需要一千美元。

content.text: So Marco, do you want to be an investor? Do you want to invest someone?
content.trans: 所以，马可，你想成为投资人吗？你想要投资别人吗？

content.text: Yes. For sure. A cupcake company. That sounds great.
content.trans: Yes。肯定了。一个蛋糕公司。听起来很棒。

content.text: I know, but what happens if I don't sell cupcakes? That's a problem for you because you have made a risky investment.
content.trans: 我知道，但如果你不卖蛋糕呢？那可就轮到你来处理了，因为你已经做出了一个冒险的投资。

content.text: That's right. So that's what happens with investors. But now if you want to attract the attention of your investors with your business plan,
content.trans: 那就好了。所以，现在如果你想通过商业计划书吸引投资者的注意，会发生什么情况呢？

content.text: I think part of the most important aspects of this plan is the executive summary.
content.trans: 我认为这个计划中最重要的一部分是执行摘要。

content.text: A summary is usually an outline of the important points of a paper or a document.
content.trans: 摘要通常是一个论文或文档的重要要点的概要。

content.text: So in this case, I could say, Catherine's cupcake company will sell delicious cupcakes of 10 different flavors to the market of five years old.
content.trans: 所以，在这种情况下，我可以这样表达：Catherine的蛋糕公司将会向五岁儿童市场出售十种不同口味的美味蛋糕。

content.text: Fifty-five years old. People will love them. She has a great secret recipe and she plans to triple her investments by next year.
content.trans: 五十五岁。人们会爱上他们。她有一个伟大的秘密配方，计划明年将投资翻三倍。

content.text: That's exactly it. So if an investor reads the executive summary, which shouldn't be more than two pages long,
content.trans: 那就是了。所以，如果一个投资者阅读了管理层概要，这个概要是不应该超过两页的。

content.text: you can pretty much get the idea of what the business is about.
content.trans: 你基本上可以理解这个生意的大概意思。

content.text: So if you want more details, you have to read the rest of the business plan.
content.trans: 所以如果你想了解更多细节，你需要阅读完整的商业计划书。

content.text: But mainly with the executive summary, you can more or less know what it's all about.
content.trans: 但主要通过执行摘要，你差不多可以知道它的大概内容。

content.text: Exactly. So a summary, like I said, is something that should be short and it should give you all of the most important information about something.
content.trans: Exactly. 所以一个总结，就像我说的那样，就是应该简洁，并且能够给你提供关于某件事的所有最重要的信息。

content.text: Exactly. And while they were talking more in depth about analyzing things and doing some research,
content.trans: Exactly. 当时他们正在深入讨论分析事物并进行一些研究。

content.text: and among those things, the girl mentioned the social economic factors.
content.trans: 并且在这些因素中，那个女孩提到了社会经济因素。

content.text: Okay. When I said we're going to sell cupcakes for my company to people between the ages of five and fifty-five,
content.trans: 好的。当我提到我们要为我公司的人群（年龄在五岁到五十五岁之间）销售蛋糕时，中文翻译如下：

content.text: we need to analyze, we need to look at those, they're socio-economic factors.
content.trans: 我们需要分析，我们需要看看那些因素，它们是社会经济因素。

content.text: Socio comes from the word social. It means where in society they are, they're upper class, middle class, or lower class.
content.trans: Socio 源于单词 社会，意味着他们在社会中的位置是上层阶级、中产阶级还是下层阶级。

content.text: Economic means how much money do they make? Do they make $10,000 a year or $100,000 a year?
content.trans: 经济手段，他们一年赚多少钱？是年收入一万还是十万？

content.text: And so the kind of people we want to sell my cupcakes to will be, will change according to their socio-economic factors.
content.trans: 于是，我们想要卖给我的蛋糕的人群将会根据他们的社会经济因素而改变。

content.text: That's right. So as you mentioned, socio comes from the word social or from society.
content.trans: 没错。正如你所提到的，socio 来自于单词社会或来自社会。

content.text: So you're analyzing these factors from society. And well, part of these factors is the GDP per capita.
content.trans: 所以你是在从社会的角度分析这些因素。而这些因素中的一部分就是人均国内生产总值（GDP）。

content.text: So we have two different words there, an acronym, GDP.
content.trans: 所以这里有两个不同的词，一个是缩写词GDP。

content.text: GDP gross domestic products. Okay. That might seem confusing because gross means different things at different times.
content.trans: GDP 是国内生产总值。哦，这可能让人感到困惑，因为“GDP”在不同时间有不同的含义。

content.text: But in this case, domestic means our country. So within a country, all of the products added up together.
content.trans: 但在这个情况下，国内指的是我们的国家。因此，在一个国家里，所有添加在一起的产品总和就是全部。

content.text: Right. And gross is basically that, just all the products added up together without taking into consideration any other things.
content.trans: 好的。粗略地说，就是所有产品加起来的总和，不考虑任何其他因素。

content.text: So the GDP is basically all the goods and services produced in the country within a given time.
content.trans: 所以，GDP基本上是该国在给定时间内生产的全部商品和服务。

content.text: And what about per capita, though?
content.trans: 而且，人均呢？

content.text: So per capita comes from Latin. Per means four or each and capita is ahead. So this is per person.
content.trans: 所以人均来自拉丁语。per 意思是四或每个，capita 是前面的。所以这是每人。

content.text: So GDP per capita means how much, how many goods and services are made divided by the number of people in that place?
content.trans: 所以，人均GDP是指该地区有多少人生产了多少商品和服务？

content.text: Exactly. So you probably have these indicators in your country or your own language as well.
content.trans: 确实。所以你大概率在你的国家或自己的语言中也有这些指示。

content.text: But that's basically it. And the acronym is gross domestic product.
content.trans: 但基本上就是这样了。而这个简称是国内生产总值。

content.text: And just to explain a little bit, if you see this in Wikipedia or in an encyclopedia,
content.trans: 当然，这里想解释一下一点点。如果你在维基百科或百科全书中看到这个内容，

content.text: normally a very low GDP per capita is $500 American dollars. And a high one would be 35,000.
content.trans: 通常，人均GDP为500美元的国家是低收入国家。而人均GDP达到35,000美元的国家则是高收入国家。

content.text: 35,000. Yeah. And that's usually per year, right? Because you, that's usually how it's taken into consideration.
content.trans: 三万，没错。通常每年就是这样算的吧？因为你是这样考虑进去的。

content.text: The time is a year. All right. So those are the words that we have for you on language takeaway.
content.trans: 时间是一年。好了，这就是我们为你准备的语言取用词组。

content.text: Now, why don't we move on to a couple of different phrases on fluency builder?
content.trans: 现在，我们不妨来学习一下“流利 Builder”中的几个不同短语。

content.text: Fluency builder.
content.trans: 傻瓜相机

content.text: Okay. So this is important. First phrase, Marco has to do with our last first phrase.
content.trans: 好的。所以这是重要的。第一个短语，马可需要处理我们的最后一个短语。

content.text: We had a business plan. So what do you do? You write up a business plan.
content.trans: 我们有一个商业计划。所以你做什么？你就写一份商业计划。

content.text: Right. And that's a common way of saying to write or to create, to work on a business plan, to write up.
content.trans: 好的。这通常是指撰写或创建，进行商业计划书的编写，或者写工作计划。

content.text: Right. So it's something that we say that's very colloquial. It's something that is very spoken.
content.trans: 好的。所以这是一句非常口语化的表达，是一种非常常用的短语。

content.text: And I can't explain why we say it. But you'll sound very fluent if you say, I'm going to write up a business plan.
content.trans: And I can't explain why we say it. 但如果你说，我打算写一份商业计划书，你会听起来非常流利。

content.text: Or why don't you write up a business plan? Right. So it would be correct to say, I'm going to write a business plan.
content.trans: 好吧，那你为什么不写一份商业计划呢？对了。所以说，我打算写一份商业计划。

content.text: Or I have to write a business plan. But if you use this phrase, I'm going to write up a business plan.
content.trans: 或者我必须写一份商业计划。但如果你使用这个短语，我会写一份商业计划。

content.text: It's just, it's more fluent, right? It's just more native like. Exactly.
content.trans: 就是，更流畅了，对吧？就是更地道。完全正确。

content.text: All right. And our next phrase is a return on investment.
content.trans: 好的。我们的下一个短语是投资回报率。

content.text: Okay. So early we talked about investors. The money that they invest is called an investment.
content.trans: 好的。我们之前谈到过投资者。他们投入的钱被称为投资。

content.text: Okay. These words are all very closely related. And when Marco decided to give money to my cupcake business, he expects the money to come back.
content.trans: 好的。这些词语之间关系紧密。当马可决定向我的 cupcakes 业务捐款时，他期望这笔钱会回流。

content.text: And he expects more actually to come back than what he put in. So that's called a return on investment. The money that's the difference.
content.trans: 他期望的回报比投入的更多。这就是所谓的投资回报率。那笔钱是差额。

content.text: So if he gives me a thousand dollars and I give him back $1,500 in a year, he made $500. That means it's a good return on his investment.
content.trans: 所以，如果他给我一千美元，我一年后还给他一万美元，那他就赚了五千元。这意味着他的投资回报率很好。

content.text: Right. So that's the, that's the term that we use a return on investment to, so you don't say to return on investment.
content.trans: 好的。这就是我们用来表示“投资回报率”的术语，所以你不会说“投资回报率”。

content.text: You see a return on investment. Exactly. It's a thing. It's a number. It's a quantity. It's something you can count.
content.trans: 你看到一个投资回报。完全正确。它是一个东西。它是数字。它是你可以数得清的东西。

content.text: Right. And well, in the end, after seeing that this business plan is not so easy, the guy said, you know what?
content.trans: 好的。而且，最终，在看到这个商业计划并不容易之后，那个人说，你知道吗？

content.text: I'm not going to quit my job and just save myself the hassle. What's the hassle?
content.trans: 我不会辞职，只为了自己省点事。那是什么麻烦？

content.text: That's an interesting word. So if I'm going to save myself the hassle, the hassle is like the problem or the hard work that it involves.
content.trans: 那是一个有趣的词。所以，如果我打算省去麻烦的话，麻烦就是指那个问题或者它所涉及的辛苦工作。

content.text: It's a lot of trouble. A lot of trouble. So I was going to cook some dinner tonight, but I'm going to save myself the hassle of going to the grocery store and buying it and cooking it by just ordering food.
content.trans: 这真是麻烦。这真是麻烦。所以我今晚打算自己做饭，但我不想再去超市买菜然后自己烹饪，直接点外卖就好了。

content.text: Right. So that's a good example. Instead of doing all the work of cooking, you just save yourself the hassle, pick up the phone and get food delivered to your house.
content.trans: 好的。这是一个很好的例子。你不需要自己动手做饭，只需要打电话叫外卖送到你的家里就可以了。

content.text: Right. And the word we change here, you can say save myself, save yourself, save his self. So you change that pronoun.
content.trans: 好的。这里我们要改变的单词，你可以直接说“救自己”，“救你自己”，“救他的自己”。所以你要把那个代词改过来。

content.text: The pronoun. Exactly. So you can save yourself the hassle or I'm just going to save myself the hassle.
content.trans: 代词。真的。所以你可以省去麻烦，还是我也是要省去麻烦。

content.text: Okay. So that's about it for fluency builder. Let's listen to today's dialogue one more time and we'll be back in a minute to talk about business.
content.trans: 好的。这就是关于流利者建设的全部内容了。让我们再听一遍今天的对话，然后我们将在几分钟后回到这里讨论业务。

content.text: I've had it. I'm done working for a company that has taken me nowhere.
content.trans: 我已经忍无可忍了。我再也不想为一个让我一无所获的公司工作了。

content.text: So what are you going to do? Just quit?
content.trans: 所以你要做什么？直接辞职呢？

content.text: That's exactly what I'm going to do. I've decided to create my own company. I'm going to write up a business plan, get some investors and start working for myself.
content.trans: 那就是我要做的事情。我决定自己创办一家公司。我会写一份商业计划书，寻找投资者，并开始独立工作。

content.text: Have you ever written off a business plan before?
content.trans: 你是否曾经写过一份商业计划书？

content.text: Well, no. It can't be that hard.
content.trans: 好吧，这不可能这么难。

content.text: I mean, all you have to do is explain your business. How are you going to do things and that's it, right?
content.trans: 我意思是，你只需要解释你的业务。你会怎么做，对吧？

content.text: You can be more wrong. A well written business plan will include an executive summary which highlights the idea of the business in two pages or less. Then you need to describe your company with information such as what type of legal structure it has, history, etc.
content.trans: 你可以犯更多的错误。一份好的商业计划书应该包括一个执行摘要，该摘要简要概述了业务的idea，在两页或更少的篇幅内。然后你需要描述你的公司，提供诸如其法律结构类型、历史等信息。

content.text: Easy enough.
content.trans: 太简单了。

content.text: Wait, there's more.
content.trans: 等待，还有更多。

content.text: Then you need to introduce and describe your goods or services, what they are and how
content.trans: 然后你需要介绍和描述你的商品或服务，它们是什么以及如何使用。

content.text: they're different from competitors.
content.trans: 它们不同于竞争对手。

content.text: Then comes the hard part, a market analysis.
content.trans: 然后是艰难的部分，进行市场分析。

content.text: You need to investigate and analyse hundreds of variables.
content.trans: 你需要调查和分析数百个变量。
